title: The picture was the vote
subject: politics
native_material: 1952 Photo Division election photographs, ballot boxes with symbols, the EVM ballot unit
hook_mechanism: a 1952 polling-room photo of picture-marked ballot boxes, echoed by the same symbols on today's machines

pick.owner_words: "Give me sample on Indian politics 30 seconds. Again its free hand, dont ask me. I wana see if you are learning from the things im giving you" (the owner delegated the pick; reverse-autopsy excluded as the last film's engine; trojan-horse flagged as retired for samples)

concept.logline: In 1952 most Indian voters could not read, so every candidate got a picture; the picture is still the vote.
concept.central_question: Why does every Indian party have a symbol?
concept.claim: Symbols on separate ballot boxes let a mostly non-literate electorate of 173 million vote in 1951-52; EVMs still show them.
